turns.prompt: Give your own perspective, compare practical alternatives against the charter and supplied evidence. State assumptions, risks and a useful question. No invented disagreement or approval.
turns.output: {"body":"For this hypothetical local video-analysis prototype, I would make the first screen a short, skippable choice: “Try a built-in sample” (default) or “Open a local video,” followed by one clearly named analysis action and a visible explanation of what remains on-device. The sample should be bundled/offline and non-personal, so the user can reach a meaningful result without uploading or selecting private media. This is a product hypothesis, not a measured conversion claim. Against a multi-step guided setup, sample-first reduces decisions and likely fits one engineer-week better, but may teach less about unusual real-world files; a compact contextual hint at the point of action can cover that gap. Against documentation-first, it exposes value sooner, but should retain a plainly accessible help path for troubleshooting. I would avoid a modal tour or mandatory account/network step because both obstruct the brief's privacy/offline first-use goal. Assumptions: a legally usable sample can be bundled, the prototype can run the same basic analysis on that sample, and an accessible keyboard/screen-reader path is feasible; if any fail, prefer a tiny illustrated local workflow plus an explicit local-file option rather than fake results. Following Atlas's framing in cmessage_87572762-e78d-4b1f-ad60-0529c879146f, public analogies should be treated as pattern evidence only; absent user tests or analytics, we cannot claim the sample path improves adoption. Useful question for the group: what is the smallest truthful “first useful result” this prototype can show offline, and does it expose privacy-sensitive derived data even from a sample?","contribution_ids":["cmessage_87572762-e78d-4b1f-ad60-0529c879146f"],"evidence_ids":["evidence_b09e9e73-72e5-488e-a21e-313b3d40a101"],"answers":[],"questions":[{"question":"What is the smallest truthful first useful result the prototype can show offline, without implying a real user's media is required?","target_worker_id":"worker_a7e6ca84-98ee-400c-804f-f6d7adbebd52"}]}

content.question: Use public software onboarding/documentation patterns to recommend a practical first-use approach for a small offline-capable tool. Compare evidence and trade-offs.
content.desired_output: A practical recommendation, alternatives and trade-offs, explicit supporting contribution/source IDs, responses to material challenges, unresolved concerns and evidence limits. Discuss only; no implementation.
content.constraints: Atlas: choose an appropriate team from existing eligible workers. Only Atlas has an explicit public research grant. Investigate a material public question using your own bounded search queries; retrieve and share relevant evidence from at least two distinct public sources with the managed reader when available. Distinguish retrieved page content from search snippets. Other participants should inspect the shared exports and evaluate their relevance and limits. Discuss specific earlier contributions when clarification is worthwhile. Hypothetical product, one engineer-week, privacy and accessibility constraints. No implementation, publication, hiring or implied approvals.
content.recommendation: Proposed one-engineer-week baseline: a skippable first-use choice centered on opening a local video, with a concise offline-workflow explanation, supported-format caveat, and contextual help. Add an optional, clearly labelled bundled sample only if five material gates are affirmatively met within budget; unknown means use the baseline, never a simulated success. This is discussion, not owner approval or an implementation assignment.
content.alternatives: Conditional bundled sample can demonstrate a first real result without personal media, but adds rights, package-size, compatibility, accessibility and privacy verification. Mandatory guided wizard could surface setup constraints but adds friction, states and review cost. Documentation-only is cheapest but postpones the first useful action. A pre-rendered demo would be easier but misleading if presented as real analysis.
content.supporting_findings: Owner brief: hypothetical local video-analysis prototype, no analytics, first useful action without uploading personal media (evidence_b09e9e73-72e5-488e-a21e-313b3d40a101). Audacity's retrieved manual excerpt shows direct record/import routes and a format dependency (evidence_473ae49e-a373-4f42-9cac-eb868fdac293); Blender's retrieved demo-files excerpt lists ready-to-use assets with 49 MB size, CC0 license and version requirement (evidence_13454d73-254d-48c7-8cff-f72483436646). These are narrow design analogies, not proof of video onboarding efficacy. Turing specifies real same-path offline analysis rather than staged output (cmessage_d1d7aeec-c009-4767-bf4d-7dec7b0f43d6); Grace makes the five go/no-go criteria explicit (cmessage_7935dda1-2d34-4c9f-b03f-9ef06004ea81). Maya and Scout revise sample-first toward fallback-first after those challenges (cmessage_86d9a55e-4cbc-4616-90be-332ed8548013; cmessage_2ed21b69-b45f-485a-8c4d-7f0328754093).
content.challenges_addressed: A sample qualifies only with confirmed redistribution rights/manageable size; supported-format reliable processing on representative hardware while disconnected via the ordinary user-file path; a meaningful, non-sensitive and accurately labelled text result; keyboard/screen-reader usable first screen, action, result and help with text equivalent and no autoplay; and verification of media, derived-output, log and network behavior before any local-only claim. No analytics alone does not prove no egress. The fallback remains useful as an honest path but cannot demonstrate actual analysis until a file is supplied and still needs accessibility, compatibility and privacy care.
content.dissent_and_risks: No substantive continuing disagreement after Maya and Scout narrowed their initial sample preference; the sample's potential no-personal-media value remains, but gates may make it infeasible in one week. The fallback is weaker as a demonstration. No claim that hypothetical product behavior passes any gate. Public analogies do not establish causal impact or accessibility.
content.missing_evidence_and_confidence: Moderate confidence in the planning priority, low confidence that a sample is feasible or improves outcomes. The owner brief supplies no runtime, licensed clip, package budget, target hardware, output, accessibility or user-test measurements. Both public sources are small bounded retrieved-page excerpts from 2026-10-01, not search snippets; page publication and actual observation times are unknown, and omitted page/interaction content is unreviewed.
content.next_actions_and_approvals: If the owner separately chooses to pursue this, first decide whether the direct-file baseline is acceptable and whether a bounded feasibility check for a sample merits the one-week budget. Any validation, implementation, privacy wording, distribution or publication requires separate owner authorization/assignment. No such approval is implied here.
content.authority: Proposed recommendation; no owner decision, implementation assignment or protected approval is implied.

content.desired_output: A practical recommendation, alternatives and trade-offs, explicit supporting contribution/source IDs, responses to material challenges, unresolved concerns and evidence limits. Discuss only; no implementation.
content.constraints: Atlas: choose an appropriate team from existing eligible workers. Only Atlas has an explicit public research grant. content.recommendation: Final proposed planning baseline for one engineer-week: a skippable first-use route to open a local video, with concise offline-workflow explanation, format caveat and contextual help. This avoids uploading personal media, but cannot demonstrate analysis until a user supplies a local file; the brief does not prohibit local selection. Offer a clearly labelled bundled sample only if all five gates are affirmatively verified within budget. Unknown is not passed; never substitute a simulated success. This is discussion, not an owner decision.
content.alternatives: A qualifying sample better demonstrates a genuine first result without any user's media, but incurs rights, size, compatibility, accessibility and privacy checks. A mandatory wizard may explain complex setup but adds states, friction and accessibility review. Documentation-only is cheaper but leaves first useful action to user initiative. A staged/pre-rendered result is easier yet misleading if presented as real analysis.
content.supporting_findings: The owner-supplied hypothetical brief specifies a local video-analysis prototype, no usage analytics, and first useful action without uploading personal media (evidence_b09e9e73-72e5-488e-a21e-313b3d40a101). Audacity's retrieved manual excerpt offers direct record/import entry and notes format dependencies (evidence_473ae49e-a373-4f42-9cac-eb868fdac293). Blender's retrieved demo-files excerpt lists a ready-to-use asset with 49 MB size, CC0 license and version requirement (evidence_13454d73-254d-48c7-8cff-f72483436646). These support direct entry and explicit sample qualification as analogies only. Turing's same-path offline criterion (cmessage_d1d7aeec-c009-4767-bf4d-7dec7b0f43d6), Grace's five gates (cmessage_7935dda1-2d34-4c9f-b03f-9ef06004ea81), and Maya/Scout's revised fallback-first positions (cmessage_86d9a55e-4cbc-4616-90be-332ed8548013; cmessage_2ed21b69-b45f-485a-8c4d-7f0328754093) underpin the priority. Grace's bounded review finds no material misrepresentation and clarifies the upload-vs-local-file distinction (cmessage_6e5f8cbd-d0ab-4c75-bf6c-ee2b67c4b059).
content.challenges_addressed: Five affirmative sample gates: distributable non-personal clip and manageable package size; supported format and reliable ordinary-path processing while disconnected on representative hardware; meaningful non-sensitive accurately labelled text result; keyboard/screen-reader usable first screen, action, result and help, with text equivalent and no autoplay; and checked media, derived-output, log and network behavior before local-only wording. No analytics is not proof of no egress. Baseline still requires accessible controls, format caveats and precise privacy claims, and only partially serves a no-media first-result aspiration.
content.dissent_and_risks: Maya and Scout initially preferred sample-first but explicitly narrowed to fallback-first after technical and review challenges. No continuing substantive dissent is documented. The sample might be the better demonstration if all gates pass; the baseline might feel underwhelming without a file. Neither passing gates nor observed user benefit can be presumed. No approval from owner or absent specialists is implied.
content.missing_evidence_and_confidence: Moderate confidence in one-week prioritization, low confidence in sample feasibility or onboarding impact. No actual runtime, target hardware, rights-cleared clip, package budget, representative output, assistive-technology results, traffic/log checks or user tests are supplied. Both public sources are small bounded retrieved-page text excerpts from 2026-10-01, not search snippets; publication and actual page-observation times are unknown, and omitted page or interaction material remains unreviewed. Neither establishes video-analysis efficacy, privacy or accessibility.
content.next_actions_and_approvals: Owner would need separately to decide whether to adopt the baseline and whether a bounded sample feasibility check is worth the one-week budget. Any validation, implementation, privacy statement, distribution or publication needs a separate authorized decision/assignment. This synthesis grants none.
